column3: The Hebrew repeats “one man” and shifts from singular “send for yourself” to plural “you shall send.”
The Hebrew retains “according to the mouth of the LORD,” rather than “at the consent of the LORD.”
The Hebrew gives “the tribe of Joseph” first and repeats “the tribe of” before Manasseh.
The Hebrew gives sending them and speaking to them as joined narrative actions rather than subordinating the sending with “when.”
The Hebrew describes the land as “fat or lean” rather than the soil as fertile or unproductive.
The Hebrew changes to singular “he came” at Hebron and repeats Hebron’s name before describing its construction.
The Hebrew says they brought word back to “them and the whole congregation,” rather than mentioning only the congregation as recipient.
The Hebrew says “they recounted to him” without explicitly repeating Moses’ name.
The cities are described as “very large,” retaining the intensifier.
The Hebrew uses collective singular names for the peoples, beginning with “Amalek.”
The Hebrew emphasizes going up as well as their ability to prevail.
